As a preparation for advanced modules in Part 2.

Program Structure
The module runs from week 5 - 9 in the Michaelmas term. In week 9, you take a test in your workshop slot.
All workshop activities are conducted online. You must log onto teams. Your tutors are available virtually during workshop time. If you need any help, you can send a message or request to talk to your tutors.
During the workshops, you must attempt the weekly exercises. If you cannot finish them during the workshop, you must complete them outside of the workshop time and make sure they are finished before the next session the week after.

title: MKTG100 Numeracy Skills
text:
Assessment
Exam or test will take place on Moodle in the last workshop of week 9. The exam will last for 40 min for 20 questions. The pass mark is 40%. If you fail, you will have a chance to take a resit – the fails will be contacted by a module leader. The test link on Moodle for week 9 test is password protected. Your tutor will reveal the password in the workshop.
Make sure you don’t miss out your examinations as they are mandatory for completion of your module.

title: MKTG100 Numeracy Skills
text:
Textbook
No textbook is needed. But if you want to buy a book, I recommend Daryanto (2020). This is a compilation book whereby its chapters are taken from Croft, Croft, and Davison (2006) and Berenson et al. (2012). The book had been used as a textbook of the module in previous years. It also contains chapters on basic statistics covered in MKTG200 Basic Statistics, which you will take in your second year. Several copies of the book are available in the library.

title: MKTG100 Numeracy Skills
text:
Excel
I assume you know how to use Excel to calculate a basic mathematical operation e.g., 1+1. To answer certain problems in this manual, I provide Excel commands. This is a nice tool to use but also dangerous. Without an understanding, the use of Excel can put you in the dark forever. Make sure you understand how to solve the problems manually before using Excel.

1.3 Order or Operations: BODMAS rule
“Operations” refer to mathematical operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, taking square (\(5^2\)) or square roots (\(\sqrt{5}\)).

1.3.1 Problem
How to work this out: 10:2(2+1) = ?
What to do first? The answer is BODMAS.
BODMAS = Bracket, Order, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Order of Operations and Priority


Symbol
Meaning
Operation
Priority




B
Bracket
\(()\)
1


O
Order
\(a^b\), \(\sqrt{a}\)
1


D
Division
\(\div\)
2


M
Multiplication
\(\times\)
2


A
Addition
\(+\)
3


S
Subtraction
\(-\)
3









Note



You work out an expression from left to right in the order of BODMAS. Division and Multiplication are interchangeable (i.e., they have the same priority) and depend on which comes first in the expression. Similar rule applies for addition and subtraction as they have the same priority.

1.6 Greatest common factors (gcd)
The greatest common divisor (gcd) is also called the highest common factor (hcf). GCD of two numbers is the number that divides them both. For instance GCD of 3 and 6 is 3.

1.6.1 Problem
What is the greatest common divisor of 18 and 21?


1.6.2 Watch




1.6.3 Exercises

Find the gcd of 35 and 100.
Find the gcd of 3 and 12.
Find the gcd of 3, 6, and 12.



1.6.4 Check Your Calculation






Excel



Type in:
= GCD(3,6,12)
press Enter

title: MKTG100 Numeracy Skills
text:
1.7 Lowest common factors (lcm)
The lowest common factors is also called the the lowest common multiple. LCM of number A (say 2) and B (say 5) is the lowest number that can be divided by A and B without a remainder. For example, the lcm for 2 and 5 is 10 because 10 can be divided by 2 and 5 without a remainder.

1.7.1 Problem
Find the lcm of 6 and 10.

Find the lcm of 3 and 6.



1.7.4 Check Your Calculation






Excel

= LCM (3,6)
press Enter
